n: In March 1838 at Far West, Missouri, Joseph Smith recorded answers to questions about Isaiah 11. The first asks who the “Stem of Jesse” is. Jesse was the father of King David.

f.g: The trunk or stump of a tree; Isaiah pictures David’s fallen dynasty sprouting again.

n: The answer is simple and clear: the Stem is Jesus Christ, the royal descendant of David through whom the family line lives on.
Next question: what is the “rod” that comes from the stem? A rod here is a new shoot or branch.

f.g: A shoot or twig growing from a stump.

n: The rod is a servant in Christ’s hands, descended from both Jesse (Judah) and Ephraim (Joseph), with great power. The revelation does not name him; many Latter-day Saints believe it refers to Joseph Smith or to a latter-day prophetic leader.

f.w: a servant in the hands of Christ

n: Third question: who is the “root of Jesse” in Isaiah 11:10?

The root is a descendant of both Jesse and Joseph who holds the priesthood and its keys by right, to raise an “ensign” and gather God’s people in the last days. Again unnamed; many see Joseph Smith here.

f.g: A banner or flag raised as a rallying point.

f.w: the priesthood, and the keys of the kingdom

n: Elias Higbee, a Church leader in Far West, asks about Isaiah 52:1: “Put on thy strength, O Zion.” What does it mean, and whom did Isaiah mean?

f.w: Put on thy strength, O Zion

n: Isaiah meant those called in the last days to hold priesthood power to bring back Zion and redeem Israel. To “put on strength” is to take up priesthood authority—a birthright by lineage that Israel had lost and is invited to reclaim.

f.w: to put on her strength is to put on the authority of the priesthood

n: The next question is about Isaiah 52:2, where Zion is told to loose the bands from her neck.

f.w: loosing herself from the bands of her neck

n: Scattered Israel is urged to return to the Lord; if they do, he will speak to them again through revelation. The “bands” are the curses of a scattered, captive condition. Coming back to God breaks those chains.

f.g: Bonds or chains, like a captive’s collar.
